#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -J solov2-tissuenet-n-2C
#   -A sada-cnmi
#   -p tier3
#   --time=120:0:0
#   --mem=200G
#   --gres=gpu:a100:4
#   --error=%x_%j.err
#   --output=%x_%j.out

#flux: --job-name=solov2-tissuenet-n-2C
#flux: --time-limit=120h

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=200G
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:a100:4
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start with 0 GPUs or the wrong GPU type/count, causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm options: -A sada-cnmi (account) and -p tier3 (partition)
# Flux accounting and queue/partition selection are site-specific; no portable equivalents.
# Performance implication: job may be charged to a default account, have different priority, run on different nodes, or be rejected.

# Omitted Slurm options: --error=%x_%j.err and --output=%x_%j.out
# Slurm tokens %x/%j are not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

spack load cuda@11.0.2%gcc@9.3.0/lrd2rcw
cd mmdetection
nvidia-smi

# Slurm ran distributed training with 4 processes.
# Under Flux, use flux-run to launch 4 ranks.
# Performance implication: if the training script relies on Slurm environment variables (e.g., SLURM_*),
# you may need additional launcher integration; otherwise it may not initialize distributed training correctly.
flux run -n 4 sh mmdetection/tools/dist_train.sh \
  mmdetection/configs/solov22C/solov2_r50_fpn_60e_coco_tissuenet_n.py 4 \
  --work-dir /shared/rc/spl/mmdet_output/All_to_all/nuclear/SOLOv2

reasons: The resource section does not request any GPUs, but the original Slurm job required 4 A100 GPUs (`--gres=gpu:a100:4`). Without a GPU request, the job may be allocated CPU-only resources and fail or run drastically slower.
The resource section does not request memory, but the original Slurm job required 200G (`--mem=200G`). On systems that schedule/enforce memory, the job may be under-provisioned and risk OOM.

The resource section does not request the number of tasks/ranks needed for distributed training. The script later launches 4 ranks (`flux run -n 4`), but without allocating at least 4 task slots/cores in the batch resources, this can oversubscribe or fail depending on site policy.
issues: The training launcher (`dist_train.sh`) may assume Slurm environment variables; under Flux you may need a different distributed launcher configuration (e.g., setting MASTER_ADDR/PORT or using a Flux-aware PMI/torchrun setup).
